name: list_connections
description: List the user's LinkedIn connections, optionally filtered by role category or interest tag. Returns compact records; use get_connection for full detail.

role.description: Role category to filter by, e.g. "Investor", "Founder".

interest.description: Interest tag to filter by, e.g. "Investors".

offset.description: Number of results to skip, for paging.

name: search_connections
description: Search the user's connections by name or headline (case-insensitive substring).

query.description: Text to match against name and headline.

name: get_connection
description: Get full detail for one connection by profileUrn or publicId, including the AI summary and any conversation recap.

name: get_network_stats
description: Summary statistics about the user's network: totals, breakdown by role, top firms, and interest-tag counts.

name: get_conversation_summary
description: Get the AI recap of the message history with one connection (by profileUrn). Returns the summary text, not raw messages.

name: search_messages
description: Full-text search across the user's message history (case-insensitive substring over message bodies). Use this to recall what was discussed, with whom, and when — e.g. 'where did I talk about pricing'. Returns a snippet per match plus the conversation it belongs to; follow up with get_thread to read the surrounding conversation.

query.description: Text to find in message bodies.

from.description: Restrict to messages the user sent ("me"), received ("them"), or either (default).

since.description: Only messages at or after this ISO 8601 date.

name: list_conversations
description: List the user's conversations (inbox state): who it's with, the last message, when, unread/archived status, and whether the last message came from the other person (i.e. it's awaiting the user's reply). Use for triage; read one with get_thread.

status.description: Which conversations to include. Default "active" (not archived).

awaitingReply.description: Only conversations whose last message was from the other person.

offset.description: Number of results to skip, for paging.

name: get_thread
description: Read the full message history of one conversation, oldest to newest. Identify it by conversationId (from list_conversations or search_messages) or by the profileUrn of the person. Returns the actual messages, unlike get_conversation_summary which returns an AI recap.

profileUrn.description: Alternative: the connection whose thread to read.

limit.description: Max messages, keeping the most recent (default 50, max 200).

name: find_stale_connections
description: Find connections the user hasn't exchanged messages with recently — reconnect candidates. Returns each person with when they last spoke (or null if never), sorted by never-messaged first, then longest-silent. Pair with create_draft to queue reconnect notes.

months.description: Stale means no messages in this many months (default 6).

interest.description: Only connections with this interest tag.

includeNeverMessaged.description: Include connections never messaged at all (default true).

name: update_draft
description: Fix a draft that is still waiting in the user's Outbox: its body, InMail subject, recipient display name, profile URL, or scheduled time. Pass only the fields you are changing. Use this instead of deleting and re-creating, which loses the user's place in the queue. Cannot change who it goes to — create a new draft for that — and cannot touch anything already sent. Editing the body or subject clears any recipient confirmation the user had given, since they confirmed a different message.

recipientName.description: Display name for the Outbox row.

scheduleAt.description: ISO 8601 time to send, or "" to turn it back into an unscheduled draft.

name: delete_draft
description: Remove one draft or scheduled message from the user's Outbox. Takes a single id from list_drafts. Refuses anything already sent, so it can only discard something still waiting and never rewrites the user's sent history. Prefer update_draft when the message just needs fixing.

name: list_drafts
description: Read the user's Outbox: the drafts and scheduled messages waiting for them to send, plus recently sent and failed ones. Use it to confirm a draft you created actually landed, to check whether an InMail draft still needs the user to confirm the recipient before it can send, and to avoid drafting a second message to someone who already has one waiting. A draft may also be held: "waiting_for_inmail_reply" means the person hasn't answered an earlier InMail, so LinkedIn won't deliver anything more until they do; "recipient_replied_since" means they wrote after the draft was written, so the user must look at it again before it can send. Nothing here has been sent unless its status says so.

status.description: Which to include. Default "pending" (draft, scheduled and failed — everything still waiting).

name: find_person
description: Look up someone on LinkedIn by name, INCLUDING people the user is not connected to, and get the profileUrn that create_draft needs to draft an InMail. Names repeat, so check the headline against what you already know about the person before using a result. You may pass a /in/<slug> as publicId, but LinkedIn often omits that field, in which case the filter is skipped and the response says so. Each result says whether that person is already a connection: if they are, messaging them is free and create_draft takes no subject; if they are not, a draft to them is a Premium InMail, and create_draft will also need their profile URL and name, which this tool cannot give you — LinkedIn omits the slug here, so take the URL from the record you found them in or ask the user. This searches LinkedIn live rather than the local database.

publicId.description: Optional /in/<slug> from a known profile URL (a full URL is fine). Narrows results to an exact match on it.

name: create_draft
description: Create a draft message and put it in the user's Outbox for them to review and send — this tool never sends (send_draft does, if the user allows it). Optionally schedule it for a time; scheduled messages may send themselves at that time if the user has automatic sending on. Recipient: for an existing connection pass profileUrn (preferred) or publicId. For someone the user is NOT connected to — a cold lead — pass their full profileUrn plus inMailSubject, recipientName and profileUrl: that draft goes out as a Premium InMail, spends one of the user's InMail credits, and the user confirms the person by opening profileUrl before they can send it. LinkedIn allows only one unanswered InMail per person: if they haven't replied to an earlier one, no draft is created and the error says when that InMail went out. Don't retry with another subject; tell the user, and wait for a reply.

profileUrn.description: Recipient profileUrn (urn:li:fsd_profile:…). Required for a non-connection.

publicId.description: Recipient publicId. Resolves existing connections only.

scheduleAt.description: Optional ISO 8601 time to schedule for. It sends itself then only if the user has automatic sending on; otherwise it waits for them.

inMailSubject.description: Subject line, max 200 chars. Required for a non-connection (sends as Premium InMail, costs a credit). Rejected for a connection, who can be messaged for free.

recipientName.description: Display name for the Outbox queue. REQUIRED for a non-connection, whose name inflow does not know; otherwise the row reads "Unknown".

profileUrl.description: The recipient's linkedin.com/in/... URL. Required for an InMail while the user has recipient confirmation on (the default), since they confirm by opening it; refused without it. find_person does not return it, so take it from the record you found them in (a CRM contact, a URL the user gave you) or ask. Derived automatically for an existing connection. Always pass it when you have it.

name: archive_conversations
description: Archive conversations on LinkedIn. Applies to each conversation and any duplicate thread LinkedIn keeps with the same person in the same folder, as inflow's inbox does. Waits for LinkedIn and reports each conversation's outcome. Needs the user's "Tidy the inbox" permission.

conversationIds.description: Conversation ids from list_conversations or search_messages (1–50).

name: unarchive_conversations
description: Bring archived conversations back to Focused on LinkedIn. Applies to each conversation and any duplicate thread LinkedIn keeps with the same person in the same folder, as inflow's inbox does. Waits for LinkedIn and reports each conversation's outcome. Needs the user's "Tidy the inbox" permission.

conversationIds.description: Conversation ids from list_conversations or search_messages (1–50).

name: mark_conversations_read
description: Mark conversations read on LinkedIn. Applies to each conversation and any duplicate thread LinkedIn keeps with the same person in the same folder, as inflow's inbox does. Waits for LinkedIn and reports each conversation's outcome. Needs the user's "Tidy the inbox" permission.

conversationIds.description: Conversation ids from list_conversations or search_messages (1–50).

name: mark_conversations_unread
description: Mark conversations unread on LinkedIn. Applies to each conversation and any duplicate thread LinkedIn keeps with the same person in the same folder, as inflow's inbox does. Waits for LinkedIn and reports each conversation's outcome. Needs the user's "Tidy the inbox" permission.

conversationIds.description: Conversation ids from list_conversations or search_messages (1–50).

name: move_conversations
description: Move conversations between the Focused and Other inboxes on LinkedIn (this also takes them out of the archive). Applies to duplicate threads with the same person in the same folder too. Needs the user's "Tidy the inbox" permission.

conversationIds.description: Conversation ids from list_conversations or search_messages (1–50).

name: star_conversations
description: Star conversations on LinkedIn. Applies to each conversation and any duplicate thread LinkedIn keeps with the same person in the same folder, as inflow's inbox does. Waits for LinkedIn and reports each conversation's outcome. Needs the user's "Tidy the inbox" permission.

conversationIds.description: Conversation ids from list_conversations or search_messages (1–50).

name: unstar_conversations
description: Remove the star from conversations on LinkedIn. Applies to each conversation and any duplicate thread LinkedIn keeps with the same person in the same folder, as inflow's inbox does. Waits for LinkedIn and reports each conversation's outcome. Needs the user's "Tidy the inbox" permission.

conversationIds.description: Conversation ids from list_conversations or search_messages (1–50).

name: list_invitations
description: List the connection requests the user has received and not yet answered: who, their headline, any note, when, and mutual connections. Pass refresh: true to check LinkedIn first (otherwise this reads what inflow last fetched). Use the id with respond_to_invitation.

refresh.description: Fetch the current list from LinkedIn first. Default false.

name: respond_to_invitation
description: Accept or ignore a connection request the user received, by its id from list_invitations. Accepting makes them a first-degree connection; ignoring removes the request without telling them. Needs the user's "Answer invitations" permission.

name: send_message
description: Send a message now in an existing conversation, as the user. This really sends: there is no review step and no undo, so only send what the user asked for or approved, and prefer create_draft when in doubt. Refused if the other person hasn't answered the user's InMail (LinkedIn would not deliver it). At most 15 sends an hour across send_message and send_draft. Needs the user's "Send messages" permission. To write to someone with no conversation yet, create_draft then send_draft.

conversationId.description: Conversation id from list_conversations or search_messages.

name: send_draft
description: Send a draft or scheduled message from the user's Outbox now, by its id from list_drafts. This really sends, and an InMail spends a credit. It keeps the Outbox's rules: refused while the draft is held (the person hasn't answered an earlier InMail, or replied after it was written) or while a Claude InMail still awaits the user's recipient confirmation. At most 15 sends an hour across send_message and send_draft. Needs the user's "Send messages" permission.

name: delete_conversation
description: Delete a conversation from the user's LinkedIn inbox, with any duplicate thread with the same person in the same folder. Permanent: LinkedIn cannot restore it. Only do this when the user asked for that conversation to be deleted; archive_conversations is the reversible way to clear the inbox. Needs the user's "Delete conversations" permission.
